statement: For integers lambda_1 < ... < lambda_N (lambda_1 = 0, gaps listed in the data file), Gaussian-integer weights w_m = a_m + i b_m and delta_m = min over n != m of abs(lambda_m - lambda_n), the ratio R = abs(sum over m != n of w_m conj(w_n)/(lambda_m - lambda_n)) / sum over m of abs(w_m)^2/delta_m is a lower bound for the optimal constant C of the Montgomery-Vaughan weighted Hilbert inequality (C is the smallest constant such that abs(sum_{m != n} w_m conj(w_n)/(lambda_m - lambda_n)) <= C sum abs(w_m)^2/delta_m for all N, all distinct reals lambda and all complex w). The data files below give R >= 3.1427910 (N = 60001), hence C >= pi + 1.19e-3.
format: text: N; then N-1 integer gaps on one line; then N lines 'a_m b_m' (integers, w_m = a_m + i b_m)

construction: reflection-symmetric gap lists: central block of gap 1 with n_0 points, flanking lattices with gap gamma_j and n_j points on each side (counts 0.11 N, 0.0219 N, 0.0078 N, 0.0027 N; gamma_1 = 0.045 N, ratios 17.9, 9.5, 9.5); weights: top singular vector of the half-size real matrix M_ik = B_ik + B_ik' (B the Montgomery-Vaughan matrix), reflected to the full vector, scaled and rounded to 44-bit integers (code/02-montgomery-vaughan-constant/e14_big.py)
ceiling: A finite explicit lower bound for C; the true constant is not determined; the best known upper bound is pi times sqrt(1 + (2/3) sqrt(6/5)) = 4.1325 (Preissmann 1984). Not an estimate of C.
